chain.label: No dedicated CTAF area or mandatory position-reporting requirement covering the Soldotna area; fragmented, overlapping frequencies
chain.trigger: 21 airports were within a 30-mile radius of SXQ, with five different charted communication frequencies... many of which overlapped; Longmere Lake was not listed as a charted seaplane base and did not have a radio frequency published; there is currently no FAA requirement for pilots to communicate on the established frequencies within CTAF areas

chain.label: No position reports exchanged between the two flights on a common frequency
chain.trigger: A postaccident examination of both airplanes could not determine the radio frequencies selected at the time of the accident; pilots may remain unaware of the presence of other airplanes even though a method of communications exists

caused_by.evidence: These accidents demonstrate the possibility for confusion regarding which frequency pilots should be using in a particular area. Further, if pilots are communicating on two different frequencies within the same area, they may not be aware of the presence of the other airplane.

chain.label: Two airplanes departing 4 nm apart at the same time flew converging flightpaths at the same altitude
chain.trigger: the PA-12 traveled on a north-northeast heading until it crossed over a highway then turned right to an east-northeast heading on a converging course with the DHC-2... They flew on converging flightpaths for about 2 minutes until the collision

chain.label: Neither pilot visually acquired the other airplane; see-and-avoid did not provide separation
chain.trigger: Because both airplanes were operating in uncontrolled airspace, it was the responsibility of both pilots to visually acquire aircraft flying in their vicinity and maintain separation from them... the inherent limitations of this concept, including human limitations, environmental conditions, aircraft blind spots, and operational distractions, leave even the most diligent pilot vulnerable to the threat of a midair collision with an unseen aircraft

caused_by.evidence: Both airplanes continued on their respective headings and collided about 0827

chain.label: Midair collision of the DHC-2 and PA-12 at about 1,200 ft near Soldotna
chain.trigger: both airplanes... were destroyed when they were involved in a midair collision near Soldotna, Alaska... collided about 0827, about 2.5 miles northeast of SXQ... at an altitude of about 1,200 ft
